Name: Human staffing at health clubs and certain non-food retail stores.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to human staffing at health clubs and certain non-food retail stores
BodyName: Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection

Summary: This bill would require that health clubs, which include gyms and spas, have at least 1 human employee on premises during all business hours. It would also require large non-food retail stores that provide self-service checkout kiosks to assign at least 1 employee to supervise the self-service checkout area during all business hours. Separately, any large non-food retail store that operates 4 or more self-service checkout kiosks would have to keep to a staffing ratio of at least 1 employee for every 3 self-service checkout kiosks. Civil penalties would apply to health club and large non-food retail store owners and operators for violations. Finally, the bill would require the Commissioner of Consumer and Worker Protection to engage in outreach and education to inform owners, operators, and employees of health clubs and non-food retail stores of the bill requirements.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to human staffing at health clubs and certain non-food retail stores 

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Chapter 1 of title 10 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 10-191 to read as follows:
§ 10-191 Human staffing at health clubs and certain non-food retail stores. a. Definitions. As used in this section, the following terms have the following meanings:
Commissioner. The term “commissioner” means the commissioner of consumer and worker protection.
Department. The term “department” means the department of consumer and worker protection.
Health club. The term “health club” means any commercial establishment offering instruction, training, or assistance, or the facilities, for the preservation, maintenance, encouragement, or development of physical fitness or wellbeing. This definition includes any health spa; sports, tennis, racquet ball, or platform tennis club; figure salon; health studio; gymnasium; weight control studio; martial arts or self-defense school; and commercial establishment offering a similar course of physical training.
Covered retail store. The term “covered retail store” means any place that, in the regular course of business, sells or rents goods directly to the public, and is (i) over 15,000 square feet in size, sells primarily non-food items, and in which the sale of food is secondary to the primary purpose of non-food item sales; or (ii) over 85,000 square feet and with a minimum of 10 percent of its sales floor area dedicated to the sale of non-food items. This definition excludes any pharmacy or food retail store covered under a local law for the year 2026 amending the administrative code of the city of New York, relating to requiring pharmacies and food retail stores to staff self-service checkout areas and impose a 15-item maximum for self-service checkout purchases to help combat retail theft, as proposed in introduction number 729.
Self-service checkout. The term “self-service checkout” means any automated process that enables a customer to scan, bag, and pay for the customer’s purchases at a self-service checkout kiosk and without human assistance.
Self-service checkout kiosk. The term “self-service checkout kiosk” means any machine at a fixed location within a covered retail store at which a customer can use self-service checkout for the customer’s purchases.
b. Staff on health club premises. Each health club shall maintain at least 1 human employee of the health club on its premises during all business hours.
c. Supervision of self-service checkout area in covered retail stores. Each covered retail store that provides self-service checkout shall assign at least 1 employee to supervise the self-service checkout area at all times that the self-service checkout is in operation during business hours. The employee assigned under this subdivision shall have no other work responsibilities that would interfere with the employee’s ability to maintain direct visual inspection and surveillance of the self-service checkout area.
d. Staffing ratio for self-service checkout kiosks in covered retail stores. Separately from the requirements of subdivision c of this section, each covered retail store that operates 4 or more self-service checkout kiosks in a self-service checkout area shall maintain a staffing ratio of at least 1 employee for every 3 self-service checkout kiosks in the self-service checkout area. 
e. Enforcement. 1. An owner or operator of a health club or covered retail store that violates this section or any rule promulgated thereunder is liable for civil penalties as follows:
(a) For a first violation, a civil penalty of $100;
(b) For a second violation committed within a period of 1 year of the date of the first violation, a civil penalty of $200; and
(c) For a third and any subsequent violation committed within a period of 1 year of the date of the first violation, $500.
2. A proceeding to recover any civil penalty under this subdivision shall be commenced by the service of a notice of violation by the commissioner, which shall be returnable to the office of administrative trials and hearings or any other tribunal designated to conduct the proceeding.
f. Inspection. No owner or operator of a health club or covered retail store shall prevent an inspector from the department from accessing any area of such health club or covered retail store during business hours to conduct an assessment of compliance with the requirements of this section.
g. Outreach and education. 1. The commissioner shall establish and engage in outreach and education efforts to inform owners, operators, and employees of health clubs and covered retail stores of the requirements of this section.
§ 2. This local law takes effect 180 days after it becomes law.
